:::{#thm-huffman-prefix-code}
#### Huffman codes are prefix codes

Every [Huffman code](#def-huffman-code) is a [prefix code](#def-prefix-code).

:::

::: {.proof}

The construction in @def-huffman-code builds a tree
whose nodes for the values $x$ are leaves:
each of them is made first,
and only the new nodes get children.
The codeword $c(x)$ is the list of edge labels
on the path from the last node to the leaf for $x$.

Suppose that $c(x)$ were the beginning of $c(x')$ for two different values $x$ and $x'$.
Both paths start at the last node,
and the same labels lead to the same child at every step,
so the path to $x$ would be the first part of the path to $x'$.
Then the leaf for $x$ would lie on the way to the leaf for $x'$,
and the leaf for $x$ would have a child.
No leaf has a child,
so no codeword is the beginning of another.

:::
